characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: The Technical Feasibility Strategy aims to demonstrate that platform-neutral and fallback-capable digital identity solutions are viable in Denmark. It controls the scope and direction of technical demonstrator development, focusing on open standards and privacy-respecting platforms. Success is measured by the creation of working demonstrators, a published feasibility report, and the credibility of the technical evidence presented. Key metrics include demonstrator functionality, security review results, and stakeholder feedback on technical viability.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy strongly supports the Procurement Influence Strategy by providing concrete examples of platform-neutral solutions. It also enhances the Policy Advocacy Strategy by offering tangible evidence to support policy proposals for supplier diversity and fallback access.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: A highly ambitious Technical Feasibility Strategy can strain resources, potentially conflicting with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy if demonstrator development consumes too much budget. It may also conflict with Coalition Building Strategy if the technical focus alienates non-technical stakeholders.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: The Policy Advocacy Strategy shapes the narrative around Denmark's digital identity infrastructure, focusing on resilience, continuity of service, and supplier concentration risks. It controls the framing of the issue and the arguments presented to policymakers. Success is measured by the inclusion of platform-neutrality language in AltID-related documents and a formal response from Digitaliseringsstyrelsen. Key metrics include the number of policy proposals submitted and the level of engagement from government stakeholders.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy works in tandem with the Coalition Building Strategy, as a broader coalition strengthens the advocacy position. It also benefits from the Technical Feasibility Strategy, which provides evidence to support policy arguments and demonstrate the viability of alternative solutions.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Focusing too narrowly on continuity of service might conflict with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy if broader European standards prioritize privacy or interoperability over resilience. A strong Policy Advocacy Strategy may also conflict with Procurement Influence Strategy if policy goals are perceived as too restrictive.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: The Coalition Building Strategy aims to create a broad base of support for platform-neutral digital identity in Denmark. It controls the composition and engagement of the coalition, spanning civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, academic researchers, and security experts. Success is measured by the strength of the advocacy position and the political pressure exerted for platform neutrality. Key metrics include the number of coalition members and the level of engagement from each stakeholder group.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy directly amplifies the Policy Advocacy Strategy, as a stronger coalition strengthens the advocacy position in procurement discussions. It also supports the Procurement Influence Strategy by creating greater political pressure for platform neutrality in procurement decisions.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Expanding the coalition too broadly may conflict with the Technical Feasibility Strategy if diverse stakeholder priorities dilute the technical focus. Building a large coalition may also conflict with Procurement Influence Strategy if conflicting priorities weaken the advocacy position during procurement discussions.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: The Procurement Influence Strategy focuses on incorporating platform-neutrality and fallback access requirements into AltID and related digital identity procurements. It controls the specificity and implementability of procurement language. Success is measured by the inclusion of relevant language in official procurement documents and reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google. Key metrics include the number of procurement documents influenced and the degree of platform neutrality achieved.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy is directly enabled by the Technical Feasibility Strategy, which provides evidence to support specific requirements for platform-neutral access. It also benefits from the Policy Advocacy Strategy, which creates a favorable policy environment for supplier diversity and fallback access.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Advocating for highly specific requirements may conflict with the EU Standards Engagement Strategy if those requirements are not aligned with broader European standards. A strong Procurement Influence Strategy may also conflict with Coalition Building Strategy if specific requirements alienate some coalition members.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: The EU Standards Engagement Strategy aims to align Danish advocacy with broader European requirements on interoperability, portability, resilience, and reduced platform lock-in. It controls the level of engagement with relevant EU bodies and technical working groups. Success is measured by the alignment of Danish advocacy with European Digital Identity Wallet materials and enhanced interoperability across Europe. Key metrics include the number of inputs provided to EU bodies and the degree of alignment achieved.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This strategy complements the Policy Advocacy Strategy by extending the advocacy efforts to the EU level. It also benefits from the Technical Feasibility Strategy, which can provide technical input to EU standards discussions and demonstrate the viability of platform-neutral solutions.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Active engagement with EU bodies may conflict with the Technical Feasibility Strategy if it diverts resources from demonstrator development. Championing a 'sovereign identity sandbox' may also conflict with Coalition Building Strategy if it is perceived as too radical or disruptive by some coalition members.
